title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, initiate a new face and within this first face, draw a single loop. Within this loop, draw a circle centered at coordinates (0.0325, 0.0325) with a radius of 0.0325 units. After completing the circle, apply a scaling factor of 0.065 to the entire 2D sketch. Transform this scaled 2D sketch into a 3D object by rotating it according to the Euler angles and translating it based on the translation vector defined in the coordinate system. Finally, extrude the 2D sketch along the normal direction by 0.75 units to create a cylindrical solid body. Ensure that the extrusion does not extend in the opposite direction. The final dimensions of the cylindrical object will be 0.065 units in length, 0.065 units in width, and 0.75 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = workplane.center(0.0325, 0.0325).circle(0.0325)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the sketch scale (if necessary)
# Note: The sketch scale is applied to the sketch before extrusion, but in this case, it is 0.065 which is the same as the radius.
#       Therefore, the sketch is already scaled correctly, and no additional scaling is needed.

# Finalize the model
r = cylinder

# Display the model

import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0325, 0.0325)  # Move to the center of the circle
    .circle(0.0325)  # Draw a circle with the specified radius
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder
